# Set SH Degree

Limits how much a splat's colour can vary with the viewing direction; lower degrees make files much smaller.

`lfs.set_sh_degree` · Splat

## How to use

Use Degree 0 for flat colour and smaller exports.\
Raising the degree adds room for detail but cannot restore discarded colour.

## Inputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Geometry | `Geometry` | lfs.geometry | — | — | Geometry you want to edit. Connect a source; an unconnected input supplies no geometry. |
| Degree | `Degree` | lfs.int | 0 | min 0; max 3; step 1 | SH degree, 0–3. 0, the default, removes view-dependent colour; higher values allow more angular detail. |

## Outputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Geometry | `Geometry` | lfs.geometry | — | — | Resulting geometry. Connect to another editing node or Group Output. |
